📌 Clipboard Hijacking: Why the Address You Paste May Not Be Yours

Main Points
⏺ Crypto addresses are long, so almost everyone copies and pastes them
⏺ Clipboard malware watches for that moment and swaps in the attacker's address
⏺ This post explains how the swap works and the simple habit that stops it


1⃣ Core Idea — A clipper is malware that monitors your clipboard. When it sees something that looks like a wallet address, it silently replaces it with one controlled by the attacker.
2⃣ Why It Works — People check the first few and last few characters at most. Some clippers even pick look-alike addresses that match those characters.
3⃣ Example — You copy an exchange deposit address, paste it into your wallet, and hit send. The pasted address is different, and the transfer cannot be reversed.
4⃣ Risk Surface — Pirated software, fake wallet apps, cracked games and shady browser add-ons are common carriers. The malware can sit unnoticed for months.
5⃣ Practical Rule — After pasting, compare the full address with the source, or verify it on your hardware wallet screen. For new addresses, send a small test first.
Final Thoughts

The blockchain did exactly what you told it to do — the problem happened on your device before you clicked send. A ten-second check is cheaper than any lost transfer.

Iran Claims Strike on U.S. Radar in Bahrain

Iranian state media reported an “enemy” strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik on Thursday night. The town on the Strait of Hormuz hosts part of Iran’s radar and communications network monitoring the waterway and has been hit repeatedly since the war began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on February 28.

The Revolutionary Guards said they struck back about an hour later, destroying a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain, home to the headquarters of the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet. 

They did not explicitly name the attacker in Sirik. The Guards called the strike a “serious warning” to end “aerial provocations and oil smuggling” in the strait and threatened a response “without limits” if attacks continued.

Neither Washington nor Bahrain has confirmed the attack or any damage. It is Iran’s first reported attack on American military assets in a Gulf country since September 2, when the Guards claimed missile and drone strikes on U.S. bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq.

Trump says Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and other Gulf states asked him to hold off on larger strikes. 

American forces can strike Iran from bases in those countries, and Iran treats those bases as targets. Qatar and Pakistan are still mediating between Washington and Tehran.

Could a familiar door make a nursing home feel more like home? In some Dutch care homes, it does.

Staff put life-size stickers of residents’ original front doors on their room entrances. Suddenly, a corridor full of lookalike doors has a few familiar faces - or, well, doors.

Called True Doors, the custom decals help residents with dementia find their rooms, feel less disoriented and reconnect with personal memories. Caregivers say they can also support independence and dignity, while making rooms feel warmer and more comforting.

Sometimes, a little piece of home is just one door away.
